articles.full_content:
The Ministry of Skill Development & Entrepreneurship (MSDE) successfully observed Swachhata Pakhwada 2026 from 16 th July to 31 st July 2026, reaffirming its commitment towards the vision of Swachh Bharat Mission and promoting cleanliness, hygiene and environmental sustainability across all its offices, attached and subordinate offices, autonomous bodies and field institutions.
The Swachhata Pakhwada was organised in accordance with the guidelines issued by the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti. During the fortnight, a wide range of activities were undertaken throughout the Ministry and its organisations to foster awareness and encourage active participation among officers, officials, trainees and stakeholders.
The observance commenced with the Swachhata Pledge administered by Ms. Debashree Mukherjee, Secretary (MSDE), where in officers and staﬀ reaffirmed their commitment towards maintaining cleanliness and promoting hygienic practices in their workplaces and surroundings.
As part of the awareness initiatives, the Ministry organised various employee engagement activities including a Poster Making Competition and Slogan Writing Competition on the theme of cleanliness and environmental conservation. A workshop on "Curbing Single-use Plastic" was also organised to sensitise participants about sustainable alternatives and responsible waste management practices.
In addition to above, tree plantation drive was also organised in Kaushal Bhawan. Saplings of indigenous tree species were planted by the all the senior officers to promote environmental conservation, enhance green cover and reinforce the message of sustainable development. The initiative reflected the Ministry's commitment towards fostering a cleaner, greener and environmentally responsible ecosystem.
Addressing the occasion, senior officers of the Ministry emphasised that cleanliness is a shared responsibility and an essential component of creating safe, healthy and productive workplaces. They encouraged all employees and trainees to adopt cleanliness as a way of life and continue practising the principles of Swachhata beyond the Pakhwada.
MSDE's attached offices, subordinate offices, autonomous bodies, and other training institutions actively participated in the campaign by organising plantation drives, awareness programmes, community outreach activities, cleanliness campaigns and behavioural change initiatives in collaboration with local communities.
The Ministry also undertook extensive digital outreach through its official website and social media platforms by disseminating messages promoting cleanliness, sustainable practices and citizen participation in the Swachh Bharat Mission.

articles.full_content:
KCC- MISS has Positively Impacted Cropping Intensity and Multi-Season Cultivation Government Introduces Several technological interventions such as Kisan Rin Portal, Jan Samarth portal, e-KCC, KRISHIKA to Streamline Agricultural Credit Delivery Process
A third-party assessment of the KCC–MISS has been conducted through Institute for Social and Economic Change (ISEC), Bengaluru, to assess the scheme’s functioning across India’s diverse agro-regions (As reported by Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India).
The main findings of the report submitted by ISEC are as under:
• Every ₹1 invested under KCC–MISS contributes ₹2.30 to net value addition in the agriculture & allied sector. The MISS has played a crucial role in reducing the interest burden on farmers, with an estimated subsidy outlay of ₹1.87 lakh crores since inception till 2024-25. The scheme has positively impacted cropping intensity and multi-season cultivation, with KCC-MISS farmers cultivating larger areas, achieving higher cropping intensity, and adopting more diversified crop portfolios across seasons, supported by reliable irrigation and concessional credit; It has improved the timeliness of input use through access to adequate working capital, and beneficiaries receiving Prompt Repayment Incentive (PRI) have demonstrated better credit discipline, thereby enhancing banks' confidence for further lending; The scheme has supported dairy and livestock expansion and promoted income diversification by supplementing crop income, reducing dependence on seasonal agriculture, and integrating livestock and fisheries farming with crop production. It has also supported Working Capital Requirements (WCR) for inland fisheries, which is significant for diversification in the North-Eastern Region.

articles.full_content:
Under the Government of India’s Skill India Mission (SIM), the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) delivers skill, re-skill and up-skill training through an extensive network of skill development centres under various schemes, viz. Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY), Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS), National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) and Craftsman Training Scheme (CTS) through Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs), to all the sections of the society across the country including Kerala. The SIM aims at enabling youth of India to get future ready and equipped with industry relevant skills including in paramedical and allied healthcare sectors.
PMKVY: Under the PMKVY, the Ministry supports training in job roles relevant to healthcare services. The major healthcare job roles under PMKVY 4.0 include Emergency Medical Technician-Basic, General Duty Assistant, Geriatric Caregiver (Institutional & Home Care), Healthcare Hygiene and Housekeeping Aide, Assistant Yoga Instructor, Panchakarma Assistant and Genetic Counselor.
MSDE has launched the Training Programme for Multi-Skilled Caregivers under PMKVY, in line with the Union Budget 2026–27 announcements to skill 1.5 lakh caregiving professionals (1.3 lakh through MSDE ecosystem), creating a professionally trained workforce for healthcare, geriatric and home-based care while opening new employment opportunities, particularly for women and youth.
NAPS: Under NAPS, apprenticeship opportunities are available across healthcare, paramedical, and allied healthcare sectors, based on the skill requirements of participating establishments.
JSS: Under JSS Scheme, various healthcare-related skill development programmes are being implemented to enhance employability and livelihood opportunities, particularly for non-literate, neo-literate, school dropouts, etc. The healthcare-related courses offered under the JSS Scheme include Basic Health and Wellness Skills (Secondary School), Basic Health and Wellness Skills (Senior Secondary School), Fundamentals of POSHAK (Poshan Shiksha and Kaushal) for Anganwadi Karya Karta, Foundation Course in Healthcare, Front Line Health Worker, General Duty Assistant (GDA), Helpers for Hospitals and Nursing Homes, General Duty Attendant (GDA), Geriatric Assistant, and Optician.
CTS: Under CTS, the Healthcare Sector trades being offered through Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) include Dental Laboratory Equipment Technician, Geriatric (old age) Care, Health Sanitary Inspector, Physiotherapy Technician, Radiology Technician, etc.

articles.full_content:

Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY), Jan Sikhshan Sansthan (JSS), National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) and Craftsman Training Scheme (CTS) through Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs), to all the sections of the society across the country. The SIM aims at enabling the youth of India to get future-ready, equipped with industry-relevant skills.
Government is actively working to expand training opportunities across the country including in rural, tribal, and aspirational districts, by encouraging more training infrastructure, better coverage of underserved areas, and strengthening of skilling initiatives through the State Skill Development Missions.
An independent third-party impact evaluation of the PMKVY 4.0 was conducted by Arun Jaitley National Institute of Financial Management (AJNIFM), an autonomous Institution of Ministry of Finance, Government of India. As per the report, PMKVY training has contributed to a measurable shift in employment outcomes for short term training (STT) candidates. The combined share of employed and self-employed STT respondents increased from 26.6% prior to training to 45.4% after PMKVY training, reflecting an 18.8 percentage point increase. Income- related outcomes also show positive movement, with 41.4% of STT candidates and 48.9% of Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) candidates reporting an increase in income following training and certification. Overall, PMKVY 4.0 has significantly expanded access to formal skill training and certification and has generated measurable improvements in skill confidence, employment participation, and income outcomes for a substantial proportion of beneficiaries.
Further, various processes have been put in place under PMKVY across the training lifecycle to ensure enrolled candidates receive quality training in compliance with PMKVY guidelines. The processes help in concurrent monitoring of training centers and candidate skilling progress in training centers. Some of the major initiatives include:
• Aadhaar based enrolment of the candidates under PMKVY to avoid fake enrolments
• Daily candidate attendance monitoring through Aadhaar enabled biometric attendance system (AEBAS) - Training centers have been mandated to install AEBAS application in the tab/phone of candidates and trainers to mark attendance during the training duration. Payment to the training centers has been linked to attendance. Recently the biometric system has been replaced with face authentication system.

The SIM aims at enabling the youth of India to get future-ready, equipped with industry-relevant skills.
In order to ensure active engagement of the industry and aligning the skill training programmes with emerging sectors, MSDE has inter-alia taken the following steps:
• National Council for Vocational Education and Training (NCVET) has been set up as an overarching regulator establishing regulations and standards to ensure quality in the Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) space. NCVET recognises the industry bodies as the Awarding Bodies (ABs) and/or Assessment Agencies (AAs).
• The Awarding Bodies are expected to develop the qualifications as per the industry demand and map them with the identified occupations as per the National Classification of Occupations, 2015 and obtain industry validations. NCVET has approved 10209 qualifications as per the industry requirements, out of which 2975 qualifications are valid and active, and 7234 qualifications are archived.
• Directorate General of Training (DGT) is implementing Flexi MoU Scheme and Dual System of Training (DST) in collaboration with industries to provide training to ITI students in real industrial environment.
• DGT has signed MoU with IT Tech and other companies like IBM, Microsoft, Autodesk, AWS, Shell, etc. to ensure industry linkages for the institutes at the state and regional levels. These partnerships facilitate the provision of technical and professional skills training in modern and green technologies.

articles.full_content:
Atal Bhujal Yojana, a community-led participatory groundwater management scheme, was implemented as a pilot scheme across 8,203 priority water stressed Gram Panchayats in 229 blocks in 80 districts of seven States viz. Gujarat, Haryana, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh during the period 01.04.2020 to 15.10.2025. The State-wise number of Gram Panchayats covered under the Scheme is available on the website of Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation at following web-link: https://www.jalshakti-dowr.gov.in/static/uploads/2026/07/415c128c8892e9a870e6398d9195742a.pdf
The key objective of the pilot phase of Atal Bhujal Yojana was to improve the management of groundwater resources in the water stressed areas of the selected States by implementing appropriate investments/management actions led by the community through convergence of various Central and State schemes focusing on demand side management. The Scheme aimed to achieve this objective by strengthening institutional and governance frameworks and by incentivizing States to implement groundwater conservation measures at the grassroots level. The key learnings of the pilot phase have been shared with other States for replication.
Ministry of Jal Shakti has conducted water body census in the country. under this exercise more than 24.2 lakhs water bodies were identified, enumerated and geo tagged. Further, under Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari (JSJB) initiative more than 1.55 crore structures have been constructed for water conservation and ground water recharge in the country. These have been geo tagged and are uploaded on the JSJB portal.
Water being a State subject, the sustainable development and management of water and groundwater resources are primarily the responsibility of the respective State Governments. However, the Central Government facilitates the efforts of the State Governments by way of technical and financial assistance through various schemes and projects. In this direction, the Government employs a range of state-of-the-art digital and technological tools not only for mapping and monitoring water resources of the country, but also for planning precise policy interventions and evaluating performance of schemes. The details of the major steps taken in this regard are as under:
• National Aquifer Mapping and Management Programme (NAQUIM) : The Central Ground Water Board (CGWB) is implementing NAQUIM, utilizing advanced technologies such as Remote Sensing (RS) and Geographic Information Systems (GIS) for aquifer mapping, identifying recharge zones and assessing source sustainability. Under NAQUIM Phase 1.0, the entire mappable area of the country of 25 lakh sq. kms has been mapped and district level aquifer maps along with suitable management plans have been disseminated to State/District administrations for implementation. articles.full_content:
The Field Operations Division of National Statistics Office (NSO) under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, Government of India is engaged in collecting information from households and establishments since 1950 which is used for planning and policy formulation both at National and State level.
Information is collected by trained officers of the NSO using hand-held digital devices (tablets) equipped with e-Sigma software and secure web portals designated for enterprise surveys. All information collected in these surveys is kept strictly confidential. The identity of households and enterprises participating in the survey is not disclosed in any report or published data. The data is used only for statistical purposes.
The detail of surveys undertaken by NSO (FOD) during the month of August, 2026 in various Districts is attached as Annexure-I. Further, for Wholesale Price Index, Purchaser Price Index, Index of Industrial Production and Annual Survey of Incorporated Service Sector Enterprises, selected units have been sent notices and are contacted by NSO (FOD) officials for data collection time to time. Similarly, for Rapid Survey of Functional Cooperatives (April-September, 2026), selected cooperatives are approached by NSO (FOD) officials for collecting the data.
The Government, therefore, requests all the citizens/enterprise mentioned in Annexure-I to kindly extend full cooperation to the survey officials and spare valuable time to provide correct and complete information. Participation from all the citizens helps in better planning and development for the benefit of the nation.

articles.full_content:
Seminar focuses on export policies, market access, packaging technologies, GeM registration and government support for MSMEs
Kolkata; August 03, 2026
To create awareness among Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) on export promotion and facilitate their integration into global markets, the Branch MSME-Development and Facilitation Office (MSME-DFO), Durgapur, Office of the Development Commissioner (MSME), Ministry of MSME, Government of India, organised a National Seminar on Export Promotion in association with the National Chamber of Cottage & Small Industries at Rabindra Bhawan, Asansol on 3 August 2026.
The seminar aimed to educate MSMEs on the Government of India's import-export policies and procedures, packaging standards and technologies, GeM registration, MSME Conclave, recent developments in national and international trade, and other subjects relevant to market access and export promotion.
The programme was inaugurated by Smt. Kalita Maji, MoS, Department of Housing, Government of West Bengal. The inaugural session was attended by Shri Surinderjeet Singh Alhuwalia, Former Member of Lok Sabha and Social Worker; Shri Krishnendu Mukherjee, MLA, Asansol Uttar; Shri Suman Sourav Mohanty, Additional District Magistrate (General), Paschim Bardhaman; Shri K. C. Sahu, CLS, Deputy Chief Labour Commissioner, Asansol; and other dignitaries.
In her inaugural address, Smt. Kalita Maji encouraged MSME entrepreneurs to leverage the various initiatives of the Government for expanding exports and strengthening their market presence. She urged participants to take advantage of the opportunities available for taking locally manufactured products to global markets. Addressing the gathering, Shri Surinderjeet Singh Alhuwalia encouraged entrepreneurs to fully utilise the schemes and support mechanisms offered by the Ministry of MSME and other Central Government apex bodies. He highlighed that strengthening India's MSME sector through manufacturing excellence and exports would contribute significantly to economic growth and employment generation.
Delivering the keynote address, Shri P. K. Das, IEDS, Director, MSME-DFO, Kolkata, Ministry of MSME, Government of India, urged MSMEs to take full advantage of the schemes and initiatives of the Ministry of MSME and other Central Government apex organisations to become globally competitive enterprises. He called upon the participants to contribute to nation-building by enhancing the export of Indian products.

Business Inflation Expectations Survey (BIES) 1 – June 2026
articles.full_content:
A. Inflation expectations
• One year ahead business inflation expectation in June 2026, as estimated from the mean of individual probability distribution of unit cost increase, has further declined by 29 bps to 4.84%, from 5.13% reported in May 2026. Firms’ inflation expectations dropped below 5% after a span of four months. The trajectory of one year ahead business inflation expectations of firms is presented in Chart 1.
• The uncertainty of business inflation expectations in June 2026, as captured by the square root of the average variance of the individual probability distribution of unit cost increase, remained elevated at over 2% for the past six consecutive months.
Chart 1: One year ahead business inflation expectations (%)
• Respondents were also asked to project one year ahead CPI headline inflation through an additional question using a probability distribution. This question is repeated every alternate month, coinciding with the RBI’s bi-monthly monetary policy announcement.
• The businesses in June 2026 expect one year ahead CPI headline inflation to be at 4.56%, down by 38 basis points from 4.94% reported in April 2026 (Chart 2). However, firms’ uncertainty of CPI inflation expectations has remained elevated at over 1.0% during February 2026 to June 2026 period.
Chart 2: Expected CPI headline inflation (%) - one year ahead
• The cost perceptions data in June 2026 indicates a mixed signal. The percentage of firms perceiving significant cost increase (in the range of 6% to 10%) has increased sharply from 19% to 27%. At the same time, the percentage of firms perceiving very significant cost increase (more than 10%) has declined from 27% to 20%.
• Overall, the percentage of firms perceiving costs ‘up significantly’ and above (over 6%) has remained around 46% for three consecutive months (Chart 3).

articles.full_content:
Chief of Defence Staff General N.S. Raja Subramani, PVSM, AVSM, SM, VSM, graces the Occasion; 19 NITs Join IIT Jodhpur's NEWTEC Initiative to Strengthen India's Higher Technical Education Ecosystem
The Indian Institute of Technology Jodhpur celebrated its 19th Foundation Day with a series of landmark initiatives reflecting its commitment to academic excellence, research, innovation, and nation building. The celebrations were graced by General N.S. Raja Subramani, PVSM, AVSM, SM, VSM, Chief of Defence Staff, as the Chief Guest, while Shri A.S. Kiran Kumar, Chairman, Board of Governors, IIT Jodhpur, presided over the celebrations. The event was hosted by Prof. Avinash Kumar Agarwal, Director, IIT Jodhpur, and witnessed the participation of Directors and senior representatives from 19 National Institutes of Technology (NITs), faculty members, students, alumni, industry leaders, and distinguished guests.
The Foundation Day celebrations commenced with a symbolic plantation drive, where Directors and senior representatives from 19 National Institutes of Technology (NITs), along with Shri A.S. Kiran Kumar, Chairman, Board of Governors, IIT Jodhpur, Prof. Avinash Kumar Agarwal, Director, IIT Jodhpur, and other dignitaries, planted saplings on the Institute campus to establish the 'NITs Island'—a dedicated green space commemorating the spirit of collaboration among India's premier technical institutions. More than a ceremonial gesture, the initiative symbolized the shared commitment of IIT Jodhpur and the participating NITs towards environmental stewardship, sustainable development, and nurturing enduring academic partnerships. The newly created NITs Island will stand as a living testament to the collective vision of building a greener, knowledge-driven, and future-ready India through cooperation, innovation, and shared responsibility.
A major highlight of the Foundation Day celebrations was the launch of the IIT Jodhpur–NIT Engineering Woven Technology Excellence Corridor (NEWTEC), a first-of-its-kind collaborative academic initiative aimed at strengthening postgraduate technical education and research in the country. Under this pioneering initiative, 16 National Institutes of Technology (NITs) signed Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) with IIT Jodhpur for collaboration across 25 M.Tech. programmes. Conceived under the visionary leadership of Prof. Avinash Kumar Agarwal, Director, IIT Jodhpur, NEWTEC establishes a seamless academic pathway for meritorious B.Tech. students from participating NITs to pursue postgraduate studies at IIT Jodhpur while promoting joint research, interdisciplinary learning, faculty collaboration, and access to advanced research infrastructure. Aligned with the objectives of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, the initiative is envisioned as a national model for academic collaboration that will foster innovation, strengthen institutional partnerships, and develop future-ready engineering talent to contribute to India's visio

NSO (FOD), Sub Regional Office, Guntur to Conduct Ongoing National Statistical Surveys in Guntur, Palnadu and Bapatla Districts
articles.full_content:
The National Statistical Office (Field Operations Division) [NSO (FOD)], Sub Regional Office (SRO), Guntur , functioning under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), Government of India , is entrusted with the responsibility of conducting nationwide sample surveys and collecting official statistical data in the districts of Guntur, Palnadu and Bapatla . Through scientifically designed surveys, the office generates reliable and timely socio-economic statistics that support evidence-based policymaking, planning, monitoring and evaluation of developmental programmes undertaken by the Central and State Governments.
The statistics generated by NSO (FOD) constitute an important component of India's Official Statistical System and are extensively used by Government departments, research institutions, policy makers and international organisations for assessing economic and social development.
At present, NSO (FOD) is conducting several important nationwide surveys under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, including:
• Annual Survey of Industries (ASI)
• National Household Income Survey (NHIS)
• Agricultural Survey
• Rapid Survey on Functional Societies (RSFS)
• Annual Survey of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises (ASUSE)
• Annual Survey of Incorporated Service Sector Enterprises (ASISSE)
• Periodic Labour Force Survey
• All India Debt and Investment Survey (81 st Round)
• Situation Assessment Survey (81 st Round )
• Migration Survey ( 81st Round)
• Survey for Wholesale Price Index.
During the month of August 2026 , field operations under the above surveys will be carried out in selected rural and urban areas of Guntur, Palnadu and Bapatla districts. The detailed schedule of survey activities and survey locations is enclosed as Annexure-I .
Authorized officials of NSO (FOD) will visit the selected households, industrial units, business establishments, service sector enterprises, agricultural holdings and registered societies to collect information through personal interviews and prescribed survey schedules. All survey officials will carry valid Government Identity Cards and official authorization letters issued by the National Statistical Office.
The information furnished by respondents will be treated as strictly confidential and used solely for statistical purposes under the provisions of the Collection of Statistics Act, 2008 . The National Statistical Office appeals to all selected respondents to extend their wholehearted cooperation by providing complete and accurate information to the survey officials. The active participation of the public is vital for generating reliable official statistics that contribute to informed governance and the socio-economic development of the country.

Catch the Rain in Odisha: From Awareness to Groundwater Recharge
articles.full_content:
Following Prime Minister Narendra Modi's call in the 135th episode of Mann Ki Baat on 28 June 2026 to conserve every drop of rainwater, Odisha has intensified its efforts under the Catch the Rain 2026 campaign, translating public awareness into tangible water conservation outcomes, promoting rainwater harvesting, groundwater recharge, restoration of traditional water bodies, and citizen participation.
Building a Generation of Water Ambassadors
Odisha has adopted a multi-pronged approach that combines community outreach, behavioural change, institutional participation, and the creation of water conservation assets. An extensive public awareness drive was undertaken across the state through 968 Information, Education and Communication (IEC) activities , including street plays, folk performances, community engagement programmes, and awareness campaigns on rainwater harvesting and groundwater conservation. These activities were conducted across multiple districts, with Khordha recording 230 IEC activities, followed by Angul (124); Cuttack, Kendrapara, Jajpur, Sundargarh, Jharsuguda, Nabarangpur, and Subarnapur (62 each); Mayurbhanj (60); Nayagarh and Puri (50 each); and Ganjam (20), demonstrating the campaign's extensive reach and strong public participation across Odisha.
Educational institutions have emerged as important partners in the campaign. Awareness programmes, induction sessions, and technical interactions have introduced students to groundwater science, hydrological processes, and rainwater harvesting systems. These initiatives aim to create informed citizens who can advocate water conservation within their communities and contribute to long-term behavioural change.
Transforming Awareness into Action
Alongside awareness generation, 905 rainwater-harvesting and groundwater-recharge structures have been completed across the state. These include 849 Rooftop Rainwater Harvesting (RRWH) structures , comprising 21 in government buildings and 828 in private buildings , as well as 56 recharge shafts designed to enhance groundwater replenishment. District-wise achievements include 330 RRWH structures in Ganjam, 121 in Khordha, 94 in Mayurbhanj, 62 in Cuttack, 54 in Sambalpur, 53 in Sundargarh, 48 in Kendrapara, 25 in Jharsuguda, 16 in Bargarh, 13 in Puri, 12 in Nayagarh, 10 in Angul, 7 in Nabarangpur , and 4 in Balangir . In addition, 45 recharge shafts were constructed in Jajpur , 10 in Kendrapara , and 1 in Sundargarh , significantly contributing to groundwater recharge efforts under #CatchtheRain
The significance of these figures lies not only in the number of completed structures. They reflect a transition from awareness to adoption. A household that installs a rainwater-harvesting system becomes a participant in local water management.
A recharge shaft creates a link between rainfall on the surface and water stored below the ground. Together, such interventions can strengthen irrigation and local water availability in areas experiencing increa

Building a Generation of Water Ambassadors Odisha has adopted a multi-pronged approach that combines community outreach, behavioural change, institutional participation, and the creation of water conservation assets. An extensive public awareness drive was undertaken across the state through 968 Information, Education and Communication (IEC) activities , including street plays, folk performances, community engagement programmes, and awareness campaigns on rainwater harvesting and groundwater conservation.

articles.full_content:
The MSME Development & Facilitation Office (MSME-DFO), Imphal organised a One-Day Awareness Programme on Branding and Marketing under the PM Vishwakarma Scheme (FY 2026–27) at the Training Hall, Government ITI, Takyel, Imphal West, Manipur, on Friday. Around 150 PM Vishwakarma beneficiaries representing various traditional trades participated in the programme.
The programme aimed to strengthen the entrepreneurial, marketing, financial and digital capabilities of PM Vishwakarma beneficiaries while creating awareness about the various support mechanisms available under the Scheme.
Welcoming the dignitaries, resource persons and participants, Shri Manoj Sharma, IEDS, Assistant Director, MSME Development & Facilitation Office (MSME-DFO), Imphal, highlighted the objectives of the programme.
Presenting an overview of the implementation of the PM Vishwakarma Scheme in Manipur, Shri M. Siva Sai Reddy, IEDS, Assistant Director, Programme Coordinator and In-charge, PM Vishwakarma Scheme, MSME Development & Facilitation Office (MSME-DFO), Imphal, outlined the status, progress and key initiatives undertaken under the Scheme. He also highlighted the achievements made and the Office's efforts towards ensuring its effective implementation across the State.
Addressing the gathering as the Chief Guest, Smt. Hannah Kamei, IAS, Director, Trade, Commerce and Industries, Government of Manipur, emphasised the importance of preserving traditional crafts while embracing innovation, entrepreneurship, branding and market-oriented approaches to improve the income and livelihoods of traditional artisans.
Shri Longjam Subhaschandra Singh, Joint Director, Directorate of Craftsmen & Training, encouraged beneficiaries to continuously upgrade their skills and effectively utilise the opportunities available under the PM Vishwakarma Scheme for enterprise development. Shri A. Loken Singh, General Manager, District Industries Centre (DIC), highlighted the support mechanisms available for artisans and encouraged beneficiaries to formalise and expand their enterprises by availing Government schemes.
The technical sessions covered a wide range of subjects relevant to artisans and micro entrepreneurs. Shri Masotmi Zimik, State Engagement Officer, National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC), delivered a session on "Enhancing Productivity through Skill Development, Market Trends, and Sales Strategies," highlighting the importance of continuous skill upgradation, changing market trends and effective sales strategies. Dr. Meitram Luwang, Lead District Manager (LDM), spoke on "Financial Literacy, Credit Linkages, and Institutional Support for PM Vishwakarma Beneficiaries," explaining banking procedures, responsible financial management, digital banking services and institutional support available to artisans.
